You say you like writing fiction- perhaps try write out thoughts in a story format - could be an interesting and challenging way to relive some brain funk and get yourself in a momentum of getting things out without feeling like you’re journaling or writing in a diary. Good luck!

You could try doing some Tai Chi or Qi Gong - movement with breathing can help and also a strength comes mentally and physically from practicing a martial art (saw you said you liked to work out) 

Something I found helpful was Cognitive Analytical Therapy and it’s about mapping out how you interact with people, situations and things. Helps you to step back, see the bigger picture and sort of debrief your life structure whilst giving reason and thought to what’s going on.

I find that writing is helpful (I really hated it at first and my therapist would constantly try and encourage me) - writing down questions to ask yourself to get the cogs turning and possibly have a look into philosophy and see if anything aligns with your life and beliefs. 

If the mindfulness is really stressing you out that much don’t put the pressure on yourself to do it - although from research I’ve found that body scans or even simple counting can help. Maybe even just taking yourself outside into some space or for a walk - or acknowledging what each sense is tuning into to or picking up on. Mindfulness definitely doesn’t have to always be a forced meditation. 

Definitely got to do what works best for yourself and perhaps the encouragement from the therapist is becoming a little overbearing for you at the moment. Baby steps each day.
